topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the course context, and outlines the core learning outcomes for understanding what causes cancer.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutation, Heredity, and Environmental Variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a genetic and evolutionary process and explore how endogenous metabolic damage, inherited predispositions, and lifestyle or geographic exposures contribute to cancer risk.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Agents and Mechanisms of Tumor Initiation and Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, chemical, and physical agents to illustrate how direct mutagenesis, metabolic bioactivation, chronic inflammation, and promoter signaling drive cancer development across different tissues and life stages.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying Carcinogen Exposure and Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the genomic mutational signatures, population biobanks, in vivo animal models, and in vitro screening assays used to detect carcinogen exposure and assess carcinogenic risk.
